Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

PACKET-01 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or an earlier reading of this leaf. This is a blind reading.

==== LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only) ====

Three faces are shown, each with one reduced overview and native tiles:
  Face A: overview image-001; tiles image-002 (top left), 003 (top right), 004 (mid left), 005 (mid right), 006 (bottom left), 007 (bottom right).
  Face B: overview image-008; tiles image-009, 010, 011, 012, 013, 014 (same arrangement).
  Face C: overview image-015; tiles image-016, 017, 018, 019, 020, 021.

Observations
- Upright orientation, two columns per face, about 31 lines per column on faces A and B. No running titles. No ruling-level gloss apparatus.
- Face A: later-hand numerals "1572 a 1573" in the top margin and a modern "4" at top right; round red library stamp in the lower intercolumn; upper right corner cut away in a curve; dark mould at the foot. A faint short note in pale ink sits in the intercolumn level with col. a lines 7-8 (ends "...nnoz" / "...annoz"?), not read.
- Face B: same leaf shape mirrored (upper left corner cut away), so A and B appear to be recto/verso of one leaf. The text runs on from the foot of A col. b to the head of B col. a ("alius plus &" / "alius minus").
- Face C: a different leaf, modern "5" at top right; top edge lost and irregular, mounted on newer parchment/paper; col. a heavily stained and abraded; col. b upper third abraded. Col. b has a one-line rubric in purple-brown and orange capitals/uncial-like letters, followed by a tall initial I about six lines high and a text opening. Several small initials on face C are touched with red/orange.
- Script: one small rounded minuscule throughout, word separation irregular, "&" ligature used inside words, e-caudata, punctuation ".;" at sentence ends followed by a slightly enlarged capital. No underlining seen.

Tentative interpretation (not observation): continuous expository prose in which short quoted phrases (introduced by a capital, often "Et ...") are each followed by explanation; face C col. b ends one such unit and begins a new one under a rubric naming a Sunday and a reading. I have not tried to identify the work.

Areas selected: all of face A, all of face B, face C col. b from line 10 down, face C col. a lower third. Areas left unread: face C col. a upper two thirds and col. b lines 1-9 (abraded; only scattered letters), the pale intercolumnar note on face A, the last line or two of face A col. b and face B col. a (mould). A UV or raking-light image of face C would be needed for those.

Conventions: (..) = my expansion of an abbreviation; [..] = lost/unreadable; ? after a word = uncertain reading; "&" kept where the scribe writes the et-ligature inside a word. Line numbers count text lines from the top of each tile (later annotations not counted). Overlaps between tiles are flagged and are NOT additional text.
